title: Sofia and Plovdiv: A Split Week Between Serdica and Philippopolis
subRegion: Sofia Valley & the Upper Thracian Plain

hook: Two cities, one week, one train. Sofia is a capital built on top of its own Roman street grid, where you change metro lines through 4th-century foundations and the mineral water still runs free from a public tap. Plovdiv is older and slower, a Thracian hill town wearing an Ottoman and National Revival coat, with a Roman stadium buried under the shopping street. Cheap, flat, unhurried and — for once in Europe — genuinely uncrowded.

snapshot.Start / End: Sofia (4 nights) → Plovdiv (3 nights) → fly out of Sofia or Plovdiv
snapshot.Getting there: Sofia Airport (SOF) Terminal 2 sits on metro line **M4**; Serdika in the centre in ~20 min for a single-ride fare. Plovdiv Airport (PDV) has thin seasonal traffic — plan on Sofia both ways and take the train back on Day 7 morning.

itinerary.title: Landing on the Roman Grid
itinerary.morning: M4 from Terminal 2 to Serdika. Drop bags, then descend into the **Serdica archaeological complex** under the Largo — a Roman street, drains and house walls, roofed and free to walk.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Rotunda of St George** through the Presidency courtyard (watch the hourly guard change), then Sveta Nedelya and the Banya Bashi mosque, then the **Central Mineral Baths** and its free taps — bring a bottle.
itinerary.evening: **Manastirska Magernitsa**, ul. Han Asparuh 67 — monastery recipes, rabbit in wine, wild-herb salads, an encyclopaedic menu. Reserve for after 20:00 [VERIFY: current hours].

itinerary.title: Nevsky, Oborishte and the Doctor's Garden
itinerary.morning: **Alexander Nevsky Cathedral** at opening, when the light is on the eastern apse and the choir sometimes rehearses; then the crypt icon museum, the strongest single collection in the Balkans.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk north into **Oborishte** — the National Gallery in the former royal palace, then the **Doctor's Garden** and the streets of Art Nouveau villas around it. Coffee somewhere on ul. Oborishte.
itinerary.evening: **Cosmos**, ul. Lavele 19 — modern Bulgarian, small plates, a serious list of Melnik and Thracian Valley wines. Book two or three days ahead [VERIFY: current hours].

itinerary.title: Boyana and Vitosha
itinerary.morning: Bus 64 or 107 from Hladilnika to **Boyana Church**. Fifteen minutes, eight people, 1259 frescoes — the Christ Evergetes and the donor portraits of Sebastocrator Kaloyan and Desislava. It is the single best thing in Bulgaria.
itinerary.afternoon: Up to **Vitosha**: the Simeonovo gondola or Dragalevtsi chairlift to Aleko hut, then 1h30 on a broad path to **Cherni Vrah**, 2,290 m, with the Sofia basin below. Lifts often run weekends only outside high season [VERIFY: current Simeonovo/Dragalevtsi operating days].
itinerary.evening: Back down to the centre for something simple — shopska salad and a rakia.
itinerary.dayStats: Sofia, 20 km round trip + 4 km walking

itinerary.title: Zhenski Pazar, Vazov and NDK
itinerary.morning: **Zhenski Pazar** by 09:00 for the produce lines, cheese counters and a hot banitsa, then Sveti Sedmochislenitsi, an Ottoman mosque turned Orthodox church.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Ivan Vazov National Theatre** and City Garden, then Vitosha boulevard south to **NDK**; the National Archaeological Museum in the old Büyük mosque if it is hot.
itinerary.evening: Last Sofia dinner. Pack for an early train.

itinerary.title: The Train to Plovdiv, and Kapana
itinerary.morning: Train from Sofia Central to Plovdiv. Fifteen minutes' walk to your Kapana or Old Town base.
itinerary.afternoon: Get the ground under you: **Dzhumaya Square** and the exposed **Roman Stadium** sphendone, then the length of ul. Knyaz Alexander I — you are walking directly above the track.
itinerary.evening: **Pavaj**, ul. Zlatarska 7 — mismatched furniture, Bulgarian home cooking done properly, no reservations, go at 19:00 [VERIFY: current hours]. Then Kapana's bars.

itinerary.title: The Old Town, House by House
itinerary.morning: Climb into **Stariya Grad** early. **Balabanov House** (reconstructed National Revival merchant's house, symmetric plan, painted ceilings) and **Hindliyan House** (1835–40, the alabaster bathroom, the Venice and Constantinople murals on the walls). Both take an hour.
itinerary.afternoon: **Nebet Tepe** — Thracian walls of the 12th century BC on the top hill, and the best view over the Maritsa and the Rhodope foothills. Down the far side to the **Roman Theatre of Philippopolis**, which you should see empty in daylight and, if a performance is on, again at night.
itinerary.evening: **Shtastliveca**, ul. Knyaz Alexander I 31 — big terrace, generous portions, the reliable main-street table. Book for the terrace [VERIFY: current hours].

itinerary.title: Tsar Simeon Garden, Sahat Tepe, and Out
itinerary.morning: **Tsar Simeon Garden** — the 1892 layout by the Swiss gardener Lucien Chevalas, the lake, and the Singing Fountains, which perform in the evening but look better empty in the morning.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb **Sahat Tepe** to the clock tower and take a last long lunch at **Rahat Tepe**, the terrace restaurant on the hill.
itinerary.evening: Train or bus back to Sofia for the flight, or fly from Plovdiv if the schedule serves.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming. Free wifi in metro stations and most cafés; patchy on Vitosha above Aleko.
logistics.emergency: 112, English usually answered; Vitosha mountain rescue is reached the same way.
logistics.weather: Sofia sits at 550 m, 5–8 °C cooler than Plovdiv; Cherni Vrah can be 15 °C colder again, with wind. Carry a shell even in June.
logistics.bookingWindows: Boyana same-day-to-24-hours; Cosmos 2–3 days; Shtastliveca terrace 2 days; trains no booking needed except on public holidays.
logistics.money: Bulgaria has moved to the **euro**, converted at the fixed rate of **1 EUR = 1.95583 BGN**. Mandatory dual EUR/BGN price display ran from 8 August 2025 and **ended on 8 August 2026** — from 9 August merchants price in euro only, and any lev figure you still see is voluntary reference. Lev notes and coins stopped being legal tender on 31 January 2026; banks exchange them until 31 December 2026 (some charge a fee after 30 June) and the **BNB exchanges them free of charge with no deadline**. Expect some ATMs and older tills to still think in leva. Cards are accepted almost everywhere; keep €20–€30 in small notes for Zhenski Pazar and village buses.
logistics.transportRules: validate a paper ticket on trams and buses; contactless taps at metro turnstiles are per-journey. Sofia's transport inspectors are frequent and unamused. Left luggage exists at Sofia Central station.
logistics.permits: no photography inside Boyana Church at all — this is enforced. Flash is banned in the Nevsky crypt. Drone use over the Old Town of Plovdiv and over Sofia's government quarter requires permission you will not get.

proTips: Do Boyana at the **first slot of the day**. Eight people at a time means the difference between arriving at 09:00 and 14:00 is an hour of standing in a car park.
Fill your bottle at the **Central Mineral Baths** taps rather than buying water. It is 37 °C, slightly sulphurous, free, and Sofians queue there with five-litre jerricans for a reason.
Take the **train** Sofia–Plovdiv and sit on the right-hand side heading east — you get Vitosha behind you and the Sredna Gora ridge for most of the run.

Plovdiv's Old Town houses are individually ticketed, but a **combined municipal-museums ticket** covers Balabanov, Hindliyan and several others for less than three singles [VERIFY: current combined ticket price and coverage].
Eat *banitsa* and drink *boza* at Zhenski Pazar for under €2. Then never drink boza again.
In Bulgaria a **head shake means yes and a nod means no**. It is real, it is inconsistent among younger people, and it will cost you a meal at least once. Say *da* and *ne* out loud.
Vitosha's lifts are the weak link. If Simeonovo is closed, bus 66 from Hladilnika reaches Aleko by road and the Cherni Vrah walk is unaffected.

raw.Walkable neighbourhood blocks (Sofia): the **Largo** — the socialist-classicist ensemble of the former Party House, Council of Ministers and TZUM, with the excavated **Serdica** decumanus and shops running beneath it and up into the Serdika metro concourse. **Oborishte and the Doctor's Garden (Doktorska gradina)** — embassy streets, plane trees and the 1884 memorial to the medical corps of the Russo-Turkish War; the quietest good-café district in the city. **Ivan Vazov** — the National Theatre, the City Garden chess tables and the axis down to NDK. **Zhenski Pazar** (the Women's Market) on ul. Stefan Stambolov — three blocks of produce, banitsa, lyutenitsa and Roma trade, best before 10:00. The **Central Mineral Baths** block behind the Banya Bashi mosque, where the 1913 Vienna-Secession bathhouse now holds the Sofia History Museum and the free 37 °C taps run on the north side.
raw.Walkable neighbourhood blocks (Plovdiv): **Kapana** ("the trap") — a dozen pedestrianised lanes of studios, third-wave coffee and craft beer between ul. Rayko Daskalov and Dzhumaya Square. **Stariya Grad (Old Town)** — the cobbled climb past Balabanov House and Hindliyan House to **Nebet Tepe**, the Thracian acropolis on the northernmost of the syenite hills. **Tsar Simeon Garden** and the Singing Fountains, south of the main street. **Sahat Tepe (Danov Hill)** for the clock tower and the sunset terrace.
raw.Transit passes and prices: Sofia runs four metro lines — **M1/M2** (the older cross), **M3** (Hadzhi Dimitar–Gorna Banya, the deep new line) and **M4**, which shares track with M1/M2 and serves the airport. A single ride is **€0.80 (1.56 BGN)**; a one-day all-modes card **€2.00 (3.91 BGN)**, or **€3.00 (5.87 BGN)** with the night lines included; a 72-hour card **€7.60 (14.86 BGN)** (2026 tariff, published in euro since 1 January 2026). Buy contactless at the turnstile or from the machine. Plovdiv has no metro and needs none — everything in this itinerary is inside a 25-minute walk.
raw.Sofia–Plovdiv, train vs. bus: the **train** from Sofia Central (Tsentralna Gara) takes **2h40–3h05** on the fast (BV/ICF) services, costs **€5.62 (11.00 BGN)** second class on the BDŽ distance tariff — **€7.62 (14.90 BGN)** on the services carrying compulsory seat reservation (2026 tariff) — and drops you at Plovdiv station a 15-minute walk south of Kapana. The **bus** from Serdika Bus Station or Sofia Central Bus Station is faster — about 1h50 — runs at least hourly and costs roughly **€8–€10 (16–20 BGN)**. Take the train: it is more comfortable, and the Trakiya motorway coach gains you forty minutes you will not use.
raw.Cultural booking timelines: **Boyana Church** is the one hard reservation. UNESCO-listed, with 1259 frescoes that predate Giotto by a generation, it admits a **maximum of eight visitors at a time for a strictly enforced 15 minutes** — the microclimate rule, not a queue-management one. Turn up at opening or reserve by phone the day before; on summer weekends the last slots go by early afternoon. Admission around €5 (10 BGN) [VERIFY: current Boyana admission and reservation procedure]. Nothing else in either city genuinely sells out, but the **Alexander Nevsky crypt** icon museum keeps shorter hours than the cathedral above it, and the **Roman Stadium** underpass has restricted afternoon access on some weekdays [VERIFY: current hours].
raw.Architectural focal points: **Alexander Nevsky Cathedral** (Alexander Pomerantsev, 1882–1912) — Neo-Byzantine, gold-leaf domes, a 45 m central cupola and the country's best icon collection in its crypt. The **Rotunda of St George**, early 4th century, the oldest building in Sofia, standing in the courtyard of the Presidency with three layers of medieval fresco under later Ottoman plaster. The **Largo** (1950s, Petso Zlatev and others) — Bulgaria's most complete Stalinist ensemble. **NDK**, the National Palace of Culture (Alexander Barov, 1981), a hexagonal concrete slab built for the 1,300th anniversary of the Bulgarian state. In Plovdiv: the **Roman Theatre of Philippopolis** (early 2nd century, under Trajan, ~5,000–7,000 seats, still used for opera) and the **Roman Stadium** (2nd century, ~240 m long, capacity around 30,000), of which the marble sphendone is exposed beneath Dzhumaya Square and the rest runs under the length of ul. Knyaz Alexander I.
